Morgan Stanley Sinks 6%, Goldman Down 6%, Citi Down 5% as Market Selloff Drags Wall Street Banks ©JayLazarin from Getty Images Signature, Vertigo3d from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Morgan Stanley fell 6% today, with Goldman Sachs and Citigroup down about as much, in a broad selloff with no company news behind it.

Morgan Stanley leans on trading far more than JPMorgan Chase, which leaves it among the banks most exposed if trading and dealmaking cool.

Morgan Stanley's earnings fell sharply the last time markets cooled.

The stock still trades well above its five-year average price to tangible book value.

Morgan Stanley (MS:NYSE) is down 6% today, and the other big Wall Street banks are right there with it: Goldman Sachs (GS:NYSE) is down 6%, and Citigroup (C:NYSE) is off 5%.

None of them put out any news. The whole market is selling off, with the SPY down 4% and the QQQ down 6%, a day after Democrats' midterm wins hit AI infrastructure stocks. JPMorgan Chase (JPM:NYSE), with $1.6 trillion of average loans, is down a smaller 4%.

The more trading, the bigger the swing

Equities and fixed income trading brought in $7.8 billion of Morgan Stanley's $20.3 billion of third-quarter revenue, nearly two-fifths. At JPMorgan, markets revenue was $10.3 billion of $50.9 billion, about a fifth.

Goldman is even more tied to stocks: its equities revenue jumped 72% to $6.44 billion in the third quarter, over a third of its $18.68 billion total. Citi's $23.8 billion of third-quarter revenue grew across services, wealth, markets and banking, and it's falling anyway. Investors are selling the whole group today.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD:NASDAQ), down 10% today, makes most of its money from trading. Transaction-based revenue was $867 million of its $1.42 billion of third-quarter revenue, on record equity and options volumes. Morgan Stanley's E*Trade serves the same kind of trader, but transactional revenue was just 14% of its wealth management revenue in 2025. No wonder Robinhood is falling harder.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Morgan Stanley, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Morgan Stanley's Analyst Ratings

Earnings have been here before

Analysts expect Morgan Stanley's earnings to keep climbing, to $14.61 a share by 2028.

Morgan Stanley (MS): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Those estimates assume trading holds up, and CEO Ted Pick said on the third-quarter call that volumes were "slower across asset classes" after Labor Day.

The last time markets cooled, net income fell from $15.0 billion in 2021 to $9.09 billion in 2023.

Investing.com -- Dutch Bros Inc (BROS) beat on Q3 EPS and revenue, yet the stock is down about 22%. It traded at $34.33 as of Nov 5, 1:15 PM EST, near its 52-week low of $33.98. The reason is the guidance and traffic outlook, not the quarter itself.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Dutch Bros Inc (BROS): $34.33 (market cap about $6.42B) || Q3 EPS $0.25 vs $0.24 est || Revenue $549.84M vs $548.60M est (+30% YoY) || YTD -43.95%

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Questions Answered

Is demand real? Yes, in part. Customer visits rose for a ninth straight quarter, driven by energy drinks, seasonal items and loyalty. Adjusted EBITDA rose 30% to $101M, ahead of consensus.

Can growth hold? Revenue growth of ~30% shows the unit rollout still works. Citi noted that management is ramping 2027 unit growth plans.

Do beats keep coming? Earnings have topped estimates for four straight quarters. Even so, the stock fell 16.81% after Q2 and 6.35% after Q1, so beats are no longer the driver.

Questions Left Open

Traffic slowdown: Company-operated same-shop sales rose 5.4%, down from 7.4% a year ago. Systemwide growth was 4.4% vs 4.6% expected. Mizuho said Q4 guidance implies roughly flat two-year traffic, not the acceleration it had expected. Read more (Nov 5, 2026)

Margins: Wells Fargo flagged higher rent, utilities and freight costs. Read more (Nov 5, 2026)

Mixed guidance: Revenue guidance of at least $2.10B sits below the $2.13B consensus. Adjusted EBITDA guidance was trimmed to about $380M from $385–390M, and capex was raised to $370–390M. Some summaries say guidance was "raised", but the EBITDA cut and the revenue shortfall against consensus are what the market reacted to. Read more (Nov 4, 2026)

Insider selling: Executive Chairman Travis Boersma sold $106.4M under pre-arranged 10b5-1 plans. DM Trust Aggregator sold $69.4M and another 10% owner sold $37M. Read more (Nov 4, 2026)

Competition: RBC downgraded to Hold in late October, citing 7 Brew and Biggby.

Analyst Reaction

Price targets were cut broadly. Telsey went to $56 from $74 (Outperform), and Mizuho to $55 from $65. KeyBanc, Wells Fargo and TD Cowen also cut. Baird said it needs "evidence of sustained traffic acceleration" before conviction returns. Read more (Nov 5, 2026)

title: Nintendo profit misses as Switch 2 sales slump; Citi sees temporary dip
detail:
Nintendo profit misses as Switch 2 sales slump; Citi sees temporary dip
Sam Boughedda

C
7974.T
7974
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Nintendo reported July-September operating profit below expectations as sales of its Switch 2 console fell sharply, though Citi expects any share price weakness to be temporary.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Operating profit fell 16% year over year to 73.9 billion yen, short of the 88 billion yen market consensus. Switch 2 unit sales dropped 41% to 2.67 million, and software unit sales of 46.95 million also missed expectations.

Citi said rising memory chip prices may have hurt Switch 2 profitability more than the market had assumed.

Nintendo kept its full-year operating profit forecast of 370 billion yen. To hit its target of 60 million Switch 2 software units, it will need year-over-year sales growth in the second half.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

"Since July-September results came in below consensus, we expect the stock to react negatively near term," Citi wrote.

The bank said it will watch the company's results briefing on Friday for updates on how weaker Switch 2 profitability will affect future earnings, as well as any plans to boost console sales.

Citi noted that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, a Switch 2 exclusive released on Wednesday, has earned a Metacritic score of 96. It expects the game to support holiday sales, along with promotion around the live-action Legend of Zelda film due on April 30, 2027.

"Given these growth drivers, we believe the shares will recover following a temporary correction," the bank said.

In contrast, Credicorp falls under the Banks - Foreign industry. Currently, this industry has 85 stocks and is ranked #160. Since the beginning of the year, the industry has moved +11.1%.

Citigroup and Credicorp could continue their solid performance, so investors interested in Finance stocks should continue to pay close attention to these stocks.

title: Wall Street Analysts Think Citigroup (C) Is a Good Investment: Is It?
detail:
Wall Street Analysts Think Citigroup (C) Is a Good Investment: Is It?
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 5:30 AM PST 4 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Citigroup (C).

Citigroup currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.65, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 26 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.65 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 26 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 61.5% and 11.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for C

Check price target & stock forecast for Citigroup here>>>

The ABR suggests buying Citigroup, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.
